exchanges.question: What has Sonatype changed about how it describes JFrog's malware detection?
exchanges.answer: Sonatype's comparison page hardened its malware-detection claim about JFrog in the most recent capture: the wording moved from "Limited" to "Very limited, not proactive." The change was to the wording on a single comparison-table cell; no evidence indicates an underlying capability change on JFrog's side. Sonatype also asserts "80% more accurate data than JFrog" on the same page.

evidence.quote: was "Limited" → now "Very limited, not proactive" (structural diff)

exchanges.question: On AI and model artifacts, where does Sonatype stand versus JFrog right now?
exchanges.answer: From the ledger: Sonatype added Hugging Face model scanning to Nexus Firewall (format-limited, per its own blog). JFrog's recorded position is AI Catalog plus Xray contextual analysis. The comparison dimension "AI / model artifacts" is flagged as recently changed (21 Aug 2026). The material distinction on record is breadth of model-format coverage — the competitor claim is scoped to one format.

evidence.quote: Firewall policies can now quarantine Hugging Face model components by license and malware signature.
